la:adj:dexter.html:
dexter, tĕra, tĕrum, and more freq. tra, trum (
dat. plur. fem.: dextrabus manibus, Liv. Andron. ap. .—Comp. dextĕrĭor; sup. dextĭmus), adj.
dex-ter, root dek-, Gr. δέκομαι, whence δάκτυλος, digitus; cf. Germ. Finger, from fangen; cf. also Sanscr. dakshinas, on the right hand, and Gr. δεξ-ιός
, to the right, on the right side, right (opp. laevus, sinister).
Prop.: ut ante oculos fuerit qui dexter hic idem nunc sit laevus,: manus,; ; ; : pars membrorum (opp. laeva),: umeri,: latus,; et saep.: cornu,; ; et saep.: ala,: acies, et saep.: dextrarum tibiarum genus est, quae dextra tenentur, Paul. ex Müll. et saep.: dextra ejus (fluminis) accolunt Deximontani,.—Comp. in signification = dexter, but spoken of two only: in dexteriore parte, opp. sinisteriore, Müll.; so, pars, opp. laeva,: rota, opp. sinisterior,: armus,: umerus,: latus,: cornu, Galba ap. et saep.—Sup.: dextimus, a, um, an ancient and rare form, in signif. i. q. dexter: dextima via, Varr. ap. : apud dextimos,.—
Trop. (perh. not in ante-Aug. prose).
Handy, dexterous, skilful; opportune, proper, suitable, fitting: rem ita dexter egit, ut, etc.,: et Marius scriptis dexter in omne genus,: quis rebus dexter modus,: tempus,.—
(Since the Greeks regarded an omen on the right as favorable) favorable, propitious, fortunate: dextra auspicia prospera, Paul. ex Müll.; cf. omen,: dexter adi,; cf.: dexter ac volens assit (numen),: Jove,: sidere, et saep.—Hence,

la:noun:dextera.html:
dextĕra or dextra, ae, f. (as in most langg.; cf. Gr. δεξιά, Germ. die Rechte, etc.; sc. manus),
the right hand (freq. a sign of greeting, of fidelity; a symbol of strength, courage, etc.).
Prop.: cedo sis dexteram,; : quod ego te per hanc dextram oro,; cf.: per dexteram te istam oro, quam, etc.,; cf. also ; ; and: dexterae, quae fidei testes esse solebant,: fidem more Persarum dextra dare,: vos libertatem atque patriam in dextris vostris portare,; cf. ; ; ; et saep.: miserat civitas Lingonum vetere instituto dona legionibus dextras, hospitii insigne, a pair of hands clasped in each other, made of gold, silver, etc., ; cf. (so in Gr. δεξιὰν πέμπειν and φέρειν).— Prov.: dextra tenet calamum; strictum tenet altera ferrum,.—
Transf.
The right side: picus et cornix est ab laeva, corvus porro ab dextera,; cf. : ab dextera,; ; ; ; : ilico equites jubet dextera inducere,; so, dexterā,; ; ; et saep.: specta ad dexteram,; so, ad dexteram,; ; Att. ap. Cic.

Div. 1, 22 fin.; ; et saep.—

Poet., the hand, in gen.: omne sacrum rapiente dextra,; .—
Trop., pledge of friendship: renovare dextras,; cf.: Graecia tendit dexteram Italiae suumque ei praesidium pollicetur,: nec veriti dominorum fallere dextras,; cf. ; ; : ne fas, fidem, dextras, deos testes fallat,.
